figures.finding: In the Republic of the Congo, as in every OHADA state, a minor may hold shares in a company where liability stops at the contribution (a SARL, an SA or SAS, or as a limited partner) but cannot be a partner liable for the company's debts beyond it, and cannot trade unless emancipated; the Uniform Act sets no age of its own for a SARL's manager, who must be a natural person, so a manager's capacity is the national civil law's (majority or emancipation).

figures.applies: The Republic of the Congo is a state party to the OHADA Treaty (its President named in the 2008 treaty's preamble; ratified 28 May 1997, in force 17 July 1999), whose Uniform Acts are directly applicable there notwithstanding domestic law (art. 10). A minor's shares are subscribed through the legal administrator; the manager's capacity follows the Code de la famille, whose age of majority is still a blocker.

figures.finding: No child may be employed in any enterprise, even as an apprentice, before 16, save by special exemption from the Minister of National Education after consulting the labour inspector or the legal representative (Labour Code 1975, art. 116); the Child Protection Law of 2010 forbids 'early employment', meaning work by children under sixteen in the family, formal or informal sector. No light-work age is set; a decree is to list the work barred to children.

sources.said: Article 68 : Sont interdits, l'emploi précoce, les pires formes de travail et toutes autres activités domestiques mettant en péril la santé physique ou mentale de l'enfant. On entend par emploi précoce, le fait d'impliquer les enfants de moins de seize ans dans le travail au sein d'une sphère familiale, dans le secteur formel ou informel.

Article 116 of the Labour Code stipulates that: "Children may not be employed in any enterprise, even as apprentices, before the age of 16, except by special exemption granted by the Minister of National Education after consultation with the Labor Inspector of the place of employment or their legal representative. ... Congo legal framework does not set a minimum age for admission to light work.

figures.finding: No Congolese national film fund was found; the fund open to Congo-Brazzaville's filmmakers is the CNC-managed Fonds pour la Jeune Création francophone, which sets no age: it takes authors from its eligible countries who have made at least one short and at most one feature over 60 minutes, and at production they must be backed by a producer in a company established in one of those countries.
